 Oklahoma City Thunder guard Ajay Mitchell will begin the 2026-27 regular season off the bench against the San Antonio Spurs, with Cason Wallace returning to the starting lineup for Tuesday's opener. USA Today reporter Clemente Almanza reported the lineup decision, which follows Mitchell's start in Oklahoma City's preseason finale.
 Mitchell is expected to retain a substantial role despite the change. According to his 2025-26 regular-season statistics, he averaged 13.6 points, 3.6 assists, 3.3 rebounds and 1.2 steals in 25.8 minutes per game across 57 appearances, including 16 starts.
 Advertisement 
 Scroll To Continue with Content 
 Wallace's return to the starting five establishes a different role for Mitchell at the beginning of the season. The guard's previous production suggests he remains an important scoring option for Oklahoma City, even without a starting assignment.
 Also Read 
 Thunder Beat Spurs as Holmgren Shines in Season Opener 
 Mitchell struggled in his final preseason appearance against Houston, recording seven points, three rebounds, one assist and one steal in 24 minutes. According to CBS Sports, he shot 3-for-10 from the field, missed all four three-point attempts and made one of two free throws in the Thunder's 116-89 defeat.
 Oklahoma City also struggled from long range in that game, converting just 13.9 percent of its three-point attempts as a team. Mitchell committed three turnovers during the loss, joining several Thunder guards who had difficulty finding their shooting rhythm.
 The Ringer ranked Mitchell No. 74 in its NBA Top 100 and identified him as a potential Sixth Man of the Year candidate. Its October 14 analysis suggested his responsibilities could expand, particularly in lineups without Shai Gilgeous-Alexander or Jalen Williams.
 Also Read

 The Ringer also noted that the departures of Lu Dort, Aaron Wiggins and Isaiah Joe could create more opportunities for Mitchell to handle the ball. The publication highlighted his ability to score at multiple levels and suggested improved shooting efficiency could strengthen his candidacy for the league's top reserve award.
 Mitchell's immediate assignment remains a bench role for the opener against San Antonio, while Wallace starts. His regular-season production from the previous campaign provides the baseline for evaluating his contribution as Oklahoma City begins its title defense.
